confirmed.title: Zone switch keeps the previous zone's output roster; Save replaces the new zone's outputs

confirmed.verifier_reason: AlarmOutputs.svelte:549-554 neither clears outputs nor dirty; save() (l.349-353) checks only zoneId, and alarm_config.go:415 ReplaceByZone is a full replace, so A's roster wipes B's sirens. confirmed.title: Removing a boot-time central never clears the Matter readiness latch
confirmed.claim: 667b8921 added `readiness.clearReady` only to the adopt-path Matter hook. Boot-time centrals get their readiness latch from a boot walk (`wireMatterCentralReadiness`), and `bootHandle` synthesises a teardown handle carrying only `detachBridge` — so removing/disabling a boot-time CCU leaves the latch set.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SPA: disable a boot-time CCU, re-enable it. adoptCentral registers a fresh unit with an empty ModelRegistry; the stale latch makes matterSnapshotter stamp ModelComplete=true, and the first reassemble runs gcVanished over an empty/partial device list, deleting every persisted endpoint row for that CCU. Endpoints renumber; controllers lose all its accessories.
confirmed.evidence: central_adopt.go:561 `h := &centralHandle{cc: config.CentralConfig{Name: name}}` + only `h.detachBridge` set; daemon_matter.go:3184-3201 clearReady lives in newMatterCentralHook's unwire (adopt-only); daemon_matter.go:3068 boot walk `units := reg.List()`; endpoint/assembler.go:751 `if !snap.ModelComplete { continue }`.
confirmed.verifier_reason: central_adopt.go:453 writes o.handles only in adoptCentral; bootHandle (:557-568) sets just cc+detachBridge, no unwires. daemon_matter.go:3201 is the sole clearReady caller (grep). So disabling a boot-registered CCU (liveCentralAdmin.Put :721) leaves the latch; re-adopt gives an empty ModelRegistry stamped ModelComplete (:3113), and assembler.go:751-771 deletes every persisted endpoint row.

confirmed.title: config export → config import destroys stored DB-tier secrets
confirmed.claim: 667b8921 made `config export` redact section secrets by nulling the leaf, but `config import` was not updated: it writes the document's section JSON back verbatim and ConfigSectionStore.Put full-overwrites value_json, so every redacted secret becomes JSON null in the database.

The stored north.mqtt password, OIDC client secret, Matter commissioning passcode etc. are replaced by null. Import exits 0; the credentials are gone and MQTT/OIDC fail after the next restart.

No dry-run/import guard warns. Stored secret is destroyed.

confirmed.title: CUxD bring-up has no ingest retry and leaks its callback/client/writer registrations when ingest fails
confirmed.claim: wireCUxDInterface registers the writer backend, the Clients entry, the metrics client and the BIN-RPC callback handlers before IngestFromBackend, then returns an error on ingest failure without a closer. confirmed.title: Device-availability transition cache is never invalidated, so a retracted availability topic can never be republished
confirmed.claim: markAvailability gates on an in-memory cache that onDeviceRemoved never purges and Start/detach never reset. Once RetractRawStateForDevice writes an empty retained payload to the availability topic (or a broker drops its retained store), every later publishDeviceSnapshot for the same (central, iface, device) is suppressed as "no transition".

The `<addr>/availability` topic stays absent, so every HA entity (availability_mode: all) is unavailable until the daemon restarts.
confirmed.evidence: eventbridge.go:786-793 `if prev, ok := b.availabilityCache.Load(key); ok { if prevBool == online { return false } }`; the only writer is Store at :793 — grep shows no Delete/Range/reset anywhere. onDeviceRemoved (:509-527) releases liveSubs but not the cache, then calls bridge.RetractRawStateForDevice, which publishes nil retained to topics.DeviceAvailability (bridge.go:1766-1776).
confirmed.verifier_reason: eventbridge.go:786-793 is the only writer/reader of availabilityCache; no Delete/reset exists repo-wide, and bridge.go:1130 PublishAvailability is reachable only through that gate. After a broker restart drops retained state, daemon.go:323 OnConnect→PublishInitialSnapshot→publishDeviceSnapshot (eventbridge.go:654) is suppressed, so the availability topic HA needs (availability_mode: all) never returns until restart.

confirmed.title: Central state machine can never reach FAILED from RUNNING — a single-interface CCU going offline leaves the central reporting RUNNING forever
confirmed.claim: centralTransitions[Running] has no FAILED edge (statemachine/central.go:60-64). EvaluateCentralState computes FAILED when no client is connected and drops the rejected transition, so a central whose only interface disconnects stays RUNNING permanently. Only DEGRADED (needs anyConnected) or RECOVERING (never wired) are reachable.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Single-interface central (HmIP-RF only). CCU reboots; the sole client leaves CONNECTED. EvaluateCentralState computes FAILED, TransitionTo(RUNNING→FAILED) returns ErrInvalidTransition, error dropped. State stays RUNNING; every later evaluation re-attempts and re-fails.
confirmed.evidence: central.go:1316 `_ = u.StateMachine.TransitionTo(newState, ...)`; statemachine/central.go:60-64 Running→{Degraded,Recovering,Stopped}; jobs.go:400 records health component `central` Healthy=(state==RUNNING) every 60s; payload.go:54 exports the same state. evaluate_central_state_test.go:180 must ForceTransitionTo(DEGRADED) first to test FAILED — it pins the gap.
confirmed.verifier_reason: statemachine/central.go:60-64 has no Running→Failed edge; EvaluateCentralState (central.go:1250) computes FAILED when no client is connected and drops the error at central.go:1316. Start leaves the machine RUNNING (central.go:616), so a single-interface central whose only client drops stays RUNNING forever; jobs.go:400 then records the `central` health component Healthy every heartbeat. Test at evaluate_central_state_test.go:176 must force DEGRADED first, pinning the gap; RECOVERING is deliberately unwired (connection_recovery.go:321).

unverified_low.title: Device-icon negative cache never expires after a transient CCU outage
unverified_low.claim: Icon() caches the empty result of a failed fetch under the device address with no TTL and no invalidation path, so one transient CCU-webserver failure makes that device's icon permanently missing for the rest of the daemon's lifetime.
unverified_low.failure_scenario: The CCU reboots (or its web server is briefly unreachable) while the SPA device list is open. Every icon requested in that window is stored as an empty cachedIcon; after the CCU is back, GET /devices/{addr}/icon keeps answering not-found until the daemon is restarted.

unverified_low.title: CallbackHandlers.Stop can race an in-flight callback's wg.Go and panic the daemon

A callback dispatched just before the deregister triggers scheduleSelfReload/NewDevices, whose wg.Go lands while Wait is unparking at counter 0 — the runtime panics and takes down the daemon while the other CCUs are serving.

unverified_low.title: Hub refresh hooks keep the logged-out JSON-RPC client after teardown

unverified_low.title: PatchDevice/PatchChannel leave a half-applied change unaudited

unverified_low.title: restartTriggerOnce documents a double-fire guard it does not provide

unverified_low.title: program-enable subscribe failure is neither counted nor wrapped

unverified_low.title: Orphan lists are read without the mutex that guards their appends

unverified_low.title: cancelWaiter decrements inFlight for a waiter that was woken by Purge/Close and never held a permit

If ctx cancels in the same instant, the Acquire goroutine may take the ctx.Done branch; cancelWaiter no longer finds the waiter in the heap, sees ready closed, and does an unguarded `t.inFlight--` plus wakeNextLocked.

unverified_low.title: Coalesced setValue followers inherit the leader's context cancellation
unverified_low.claim: The coalescer leader runs fn with its own ctx; followers block on call.done and return the leader's error. A leader whose caller disconnects fails every follower with context.Canceled even though their own contexts are alive.

The browser aborts the REST request, cancelling the leader's ctx; the MQTT command receives "context canceled" and reports a failed write although the value may already have reached the CCU.

unverified_low.title: Coalescer.Clear names InterfaceClient.Close as its caller, but Close never calls it

unverified_low.title: out-of-scope: connection-check comment claims the probe always reaches the CCU, but it is not a bypass op
unverified_low.claim: The check_connection job comment states "`ping` is on the breaker's bypass list, so this is the one call that always reaches the CCU". CheckConnectionAvailability deliberately issues the probe under the operation id "check_connection", which is not in bypassOps, so an OPEN breaker sheds it without any wire traffic.

unverified_low.evidence: jobs.go:476-479 comment; interface_client.go:889-911 — RecordPing(token) then `c.cfg.Circuit.Do(ctx, "check_connection", …)`, with the in-code note "operation name \"check_connection\" is deliberately NOT on the bypass list"; circuit.go:82-91 bypassOps.

unverified_low.title: ParamsetStore doc comments describe an in-memory cache and a method that do not exist

unverified_low.evidence: paramsets.go:46-49 `type ParamsetStore struct { db *sql.DB; // cache[deviceAddress][parameter][channelNo] }`; paramsets.go:62-65, 282-289, 317-319; `grep IsInMultipleChannels` finds no definition.

unverified_low.title: Open's wipe step is documented as non-fatal but aborts the daemon

unverified_low.title: Recorder.isRecording is never set, so the double-start guard and is_recording metadata are dead

unverified_low.title: GetDiagnostics reports the ten OLDEST incidents as "recent_incidents"
unverified_low.claim: GetAllIncidents returns rows ordered by last_seen DESC (newest first), but GetDiagnostics takes the tail slice `all[len(all)-10:]`, which is the ten oldest rows, and publishes them under the key "recent_incidents".
